title: Short Stuff: POW Olympics
summary: Short Stuff episode on POW Olympics, the prisoner-of-war sporting competitions held during and around World War II and later. The hosts focus on the 1944 Olympics at Oflag VIII-C in Woldenburg (Wałdenburg/Waldenburg), western Poland, held with Nazi permission for Polish officer POWs, and mention the Nazi-canceled 1940 Tokyo/Helsinki games, the secret 1940 International Prisoner of War Games at Lamsdorf-area camp (called Langfasa in the transcript), and the 1952 POW Olympics held by China at a Korean War camp. They discuss events that were banned (archery, fencing, javelin, boxing), the 1981 film Victory, and the fact that Olympics awarded art medals from 1912 to 1952.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts open the short episode with playful banter about the POW Olympics topic.

segments.title: Nazi treatment of Polish officer POWs at Woldenburg
segments.summary: Chuck describes the 1944 setting at Voldenbruke (Woldenburg) in western Poland, where Polish military officers were held. The hosts discuss the Nazis claiming they followed the Geneva Convention, contrasting the camp with Russian prison camps, and the camp being an officers' camp called Oflag.

segments.title: Other POW Olympics: 1952 Korea and 1940 games
segments.summary: Hosts note the 1944 Woldenburg Games were permitted by German captors and compare them to a 1952 POW Olympics held by the Chinese at a Korean War camp. They then discuss the 1940 planned games in Tokyo, moved to Helsinki and canceled, and a secret 1940 International Prisoner of War Games at a German camp.

segments.title: Woldenburg events and banned sports
segments.summary: Hosts describe the Woldenburg Games following Olympic events such as soccer, handball, basketball and track and field, while archery, fencing, javelin and boxing were ruled out over safety and trust concerns.

segments.title: Victory film and The Longest Yard
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the 1981 soccer film Victory, which fictionalizes a match between Nazis and POWs with an escape plan, with Pele in the cast. They briefly debate whether The Longest Yard includes an escape plot.

segments.title: Pele as a POW and Olympic art medals
segments.summary: Hosts discuss Pele's supposed POW status and note that the Olympics awarded medals for art works from 1912 to 1952, including sculpture and painting, which were held alongside sports at Woldenburg in 1944.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode and give the iHeartRadio podcast promo.
